title: Norm-continuous reconstruction from finite free internal actions
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $k^s/k$ a separable closure, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}k^s$, and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its Krull topology. Work on sites small in compatible coefficient universes [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $\underline G(P)=C(P,G)$ for profinite $P$, and $T[P]=\varprojlim_i\coprod_{P_i}T$ over finite quotients [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. For a commutative condensed ring $R$ put $R_T=p_T^*R$, use internal module categories and ordinary unbounded derived categories, and write $\mathcal A_G(R)$ for internal $R$-modules with $\underline G$-action [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with its norm topology, and now put $R(P)=C(P,E)$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Suppose given a ringed-topos field presentation over the condensed topos: an additive equivalence $E_R:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_s}\simeq\mathcal A_G(R)$ with $(E_RN)(P)=N(\bar s[P])$ naturally in profinite $P$, with the regular ring comparison $E_R(R_s)\cong R$ (trivial action), and whose composite with forgetting the action is identified with restriction to $\bar s$ followed by $L\mapsto(P\mapsto L(\bar s[P]))$. Then its restriction to finite-rank lisse modules [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] has the following explicit reconstruction, in the norm-continuous categories of [def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data].

A module $N$ is lisse exactly when the underlying condensed module of $E_RN$ is isomorphic to $R^{\oplus n}$ for some finite $n\geq0$. A trivialization over the separably closed field may be taken on a nonempty profinite chart $P\to *$ and pulled back along a chosen $x:*\to P$, giving this finite free module. Conversely such a free underlying module trivializes $N$ on the covering $\bar s\to s$. The identification $R(P)^n=C(P,E^n)$ is coordinatewise. Every finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-space $W$ is homeomorphic by any linear basis to $E^n$.

For each $n$, internal $\underline G$-linear actions on $R^n$ are in bijection with continuous matrix homomorphisms $A:G\to\operatorname{GL}_n(E)$, where continuity is for the matrix topology induced by the norm topology of $E$. The bijection sends an internal action to the $n^2$ coordinate functions obtained by applying its operation at $G$ to $\operatorname{id}_G\in C(G,G)$ and to the constant basis vectors. The group laws give $A(1)=1$, $A(gh)=A(g)A(h)$. For every profinite $P$, variable element $g\in C(P,G)$ and section $w\in C(P,E^n)$, the action is
$$(g\cdot w)(p)=A(g(p))w(p).$$
Conversely this formula defines an internal action from every continuous $E$-linear norm-topological action; the two constructions are inverse. The associated joint action $G\times E^n\to E^n$ is continuous.

An internal $R$-linear map $R^n\to R^m$ is uniquely a constant matrix $B\in\operatorname{Mat}_{m\times n}(E)$, determined at $*$ on the basis and acting pointwise at every $P$. It is equivariant exactly when $BA(g)=A'(g)B$ for all $g\in G$. These are precisely the continuous equivariant $E$-linear maps. Therefore $E_R$ restricts to an equivalence between lisse $R_s$-modules and finite-dimensional norm-topological continuous $E$-representations of $G$, realized by $W\mapsto C(-,W)$, preserving every variable scalar, variable group action, test restriction and equivariant linear map. Rank zero, empty profinite tests, and $G=1$ are included; the norm topology is never replaced by the discrete topology.

proof.text: Write $v:\bar s\to s$ and $M=U(E_RN)$ for the underlying condensed module. By [lem-sfb-field-separable-cech-coordinates], $v$ is a pro-etale cover and every lisse module over $\bar s$ is finite free. Lisseness pulls back by its covering definition [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Apply [lem-sfb-field-action-topos-coefficients] to the separably closed field $k^s$ itself (trivial Galois group): $\Phi:L\mapsto(P\mapsto L(\bar s[P]))$ is an equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(\bar s_{\mathrm{proet}})\simeq\operatorname{Cond}$ with $\Phi(R_{\bar s})\cong R$ as rings, so it is an equivalence of module categories $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_{\bar s}}\simeq\operatorname{Mod}_R$ preserving finite sums. By hypothesis $M\cong\Phi(N|_{\bar s})$. Lisse $N$ therefore gives $M\cong\Phi(R_{\bar s})^n\cong R^n$. Conversely $M\cong R^n$ gives, by full faithfulness of $\Phi$, $N|_{\bar s}\cong R_{\bar s}^n$, so the single cover $v$ witnesses lisseness. For the chart clause one can take $P=*$ after this trivialization. More generally any trivializing nonempty profinite chart $P\to *$ has a section $x:*\to P$ obtained by choosing a point; pulling its trivialization back along $x$ gives the same finite-free conclusion. This uses finite rank, including rank zero, and no finiteness condition on $k$.

source.place: Example 4.1.10 and Definition 6.8.3; agent expansion of the finite-free geometric restriction criterion

proof.text: The map $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)\mapsto(p\mapsto(f_1(p),\ldots,f_n(p)))$ identifies $R(P)^n$ with $C(P,E^n)$: a map into the finite product is continuous exactly when its coordinates are. For a basis $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of a norm-topological finite-dimensional $E$-space $W$, the inverse linear maps $E^n\to W$, $(a_j)\mapsto\sum_j a_jb_j$, and $W\to E^n$ are both continuous by [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous]. Its field hypotheses hold for this finite normed extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, as its statement explicitly includes; both spaces are Hausdorff and finite dimensional. Thus each basis is a homeomorphism. Postcomposition by these inverse maps identifies $C(P,W)$ with $R(P)^n$, naturally in $P$ and pointwise scalars.

source.place: Section 4.3 and the finite-dimensional topological linear algebra in Corollary 6.8.5; agent coordinate argument

proof.text: Use the sectionwise natural linear operations defining internal actions [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. If $\alpha$ is an action on $R^n$, let $e_j$ denote its constant basis sections and set $a_{ij}=\operatorname{pr}_i(\alpha_G(\operatorname{id}_G,e_j))\in R(G)=C(G,E)$. Here $G$ is a profinite test. Define $A(g)_{ij}=a_{ij}(g)$. All entries are continuous by their membership in $R(G)$, hence $A:G\to\operatorname{Mat}_n(E)$ is continuous for the finite product matrix topology. These formulas also make sense for the empty basis.

source.place: Section 4.3, point presentation; explicit extraction of matrix entries from the internal action

proof.text: For any continuous $g:P\to G$, naturality of $\alpha$ along the test map $g$ gives $\alpha_P(g,e_j)=g^*\alpha_G(\operatorname{id}_G,e_j)$. Write $w=\sum_jw_je_j$ with $w_j\in R(P)$. Linearity in the second variable now gives $\alpha_P(g,w)=\sum_jw_j\alpha_P(g,e_j)$, so at every $p\in P$ this is $A(g(p))w(p)$. Thus the extracted entries determine the entire internal action, including variable scalars, rather than just its values on constant vectors.

source.place: Section 4.3; agent naturality and finite-basis calculation

proof.text: Apply the action identities at the point test to $g,h\in G$ and the vectors $e_j$. They give $A(1)e_j=e_j$ and $A(gh)e_j=A(g)A(h)e_j$ for every $j$, hence $A(1)=I$ and $A(gh)=A(g)A(h)$. Taking $h=g^{-1}$ shows that $A(g)$ is invertible. Since $A$ is continuous as a matrix-valued map and its values lie in $\operatorname{GL}_n(E)$, it is continuous for the specified induced topology on that subspace. This is the continuous matrix representation of [def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data].

source.place: Section 4.3 and Definition 6.8.3; agent verification of the group and continuity laws

proof.text: Conversely, let $A:G\to\operatorname{GL}_n(E)$ have continuous entries and satisfy the group laws. Define $\alpha_P(g,w)_i=\sum_j(a_{ij}\circ g)w_j$ in $R(P)$. Finite sums and products of continuous $E$-valued functions are continuous [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]; composition with $f:Q\to P$ gives $f^*\alpha_P(g,w)=\alpha_Q(g\circ f,f^*w)$. The matrix identities give the group laws and the displayed sum gives $R(P)$-linearity, exactly the operations of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Extraction at $(G,\operatorname{id}_G,e_j)$ returns $a_{ij}$, while step 4 returns every original $\alpha_P$, so the constructions are inverse. Moreover $(g,v)\mapsto\sum_j a_{ij}(g)v_j$ is continuous on $G\times E^n$ for each $i$, proving joint continuity. Conversely a jointly continuous linear action has continuous entries by restriction to the fixed vectors $e_j$.

source.place: Section 4.3, continuous topological group modules; explicit inverse construction

proof.text: Let $\phi:R^n\to R^m$ be an internal linear map and let the $j$th column of $B$ be $\phi_*(e_j)\in E^m$. Naturality along $P\to *$ makes $\phi_P(e_j)$ this constant column, and $R(P)$-linearity gives $\phi_P(w)=\sum_jw_jB_j=Bw$. Conversely this formula is linear and commutes with every test restriction. For the actions above, equivariance is precisely $BA(g)=A'(g)B$: necessity follows at $*$ on each $e_j$, and sufficiency follows pointwise from step 4 for every variable $g:P\to G$. Each such linear map on finite-dimensional $E$-spaces is continuous by [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous]. Composition and identities are ordinary matrix multiplication and identity matrices.

source.place: Section 4.3 and finite-dimensional topological linear algebra in Corollary 6.8.5; agent calculation of all morphisms

proof.text: Steps 3--7 give mutually inverse descriptions of actions and arrows on finite-free underlying condensed modules. For any $W$ in [def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data], choose a basis and use step 2 to identify $C(-,W)$ with $R^n$; the coordinate action of step 6 is exactly $(g\cdot w)(p)=g(p)\cdot w(p)$. A change of basis is an invertible constant matrix and is an intertwiner by step 7, so these identifications are natural and independent of the chosen coordinates up to the specified linear isomorphism. Since $E_R$ is an equivalence and, by step 1, $N$ is lisse exactly when $E_RN$ has finite-free underlying module, $E_R$ restricts to an equivalence from lisse modules onto the full subcategory of $\mathcal A_G(R)$ with finite-free underlying module; every $C(-,W)$ with the action of step 6 lies in it. Composing gives the asserted equivalence. The formulas preserve addition, constant and variable scalars, all test restrictions and equivariant maps, and send the regular module to the trivial representation on $E$. When $n=0$ all sums and columns are empty and the unique action is the zero-dimensional representation; when $P=\varnothing$ each section module has one element and all equations hold; when $G=1$ the group law forces the identity action. All continuous functions throughout use the original norm topology.
